newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemalan official predicts 8 pct inflation in 97.
newsitem.headline: Guatemalan official predicts 8 pct inflation in 97.

text.p: Guatemala's 1997 inflation is estimated at eight percent, or a decline of about 1.5 percentage points from 1996, Mario Jacobs, the new head of the National Statistics Institute, said on Thursday.
Large supplies of fresh produce and a strong quetzal against the dollar have kept Guatemalan inflation low, he said.
"We are going to be at least one and a half percentage points lower than last year. We are definitely going to be around eight percent," Jacobs told Reuters.
Annual accumulated inflation at the end of 1996 was 10.85 percent.
Jacobs said year-on-year inflation was 8.96 percent as of June 30, compared to 9.61 percent the same date last year.
One of the biggest factors in the lower inflation rate was food prices, to some extent a seasonal factor, he said. When the rainy season ends in October, food prices will rise again, he added.
Jacobs said the exchange rate has also affected the consumer price index.
"We do not have pressure in relation to the dollar. The dollar is another product like any other, and the price of the dollar has come down," Jacobs said.
On Thursday the Guatemalan quetzal was trading at 5.97973/ 5.99069 to the dollar.
